domain: Religious Studies / Jewish Law / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of the 1,900-year continuous study of Temple sacrifice laws (Kodashim) without practical performance since 70 CE. The study-as-exercise reading treats ongoing study as legitimate occupation of the commitment kernel. The performance-only reading treats non-performable law as ceremonial husk. This contest collapses the distinction between exercising a commitment and archiving its symbolic form, positioning at the D1/D4 boundary between functioning and absent drift mechanisms.

key_entities: Mishnah Kodashim (codified sacrifice law, ~200 CE, fourth of six Mishnaic orders)
Second Temple (destroyed 70 CE, material prerequisite for sacrifice performance)
Rabbinic authority structure (claims interpretive legitimacy via unbroken study chain)
Performance practitioners (hypothetical: those who would execute if Temple rebuilt)
Study practitioners (actual: scholars transmitting knowledge without performance)
key_tensions: Study continuity vs performance absence (1,900 years of transmission with zero enactment)
Commitment occupation vs symbolic preservation (is continuous study maintenance or memorial?)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Temple sacrifice law (Kodashim) as divine command requiring specific ritual performance at specific location
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive authority grounded in claimed unbroken transmission chain (Oral Torah) from Sinai revelation
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: D1 (Revision Denial) collapsing into D4 (Ceremonial Husk)

readings.commitment: Continuous study of sacrifice law constitutes legitimate occupation of the divine command kernel even without performance
readings.authority_grounding: Talmudic principle 'studying the laws of sacrifice is equivalent to offering sacrifice' (b. Menachot 110a); study preserves the chain of transmission
readings.expected_structural_delta: Study itself becomes the constraint's victim set (scholars must maintain competence); beneficiary is rabbinic authority structure claiming legitimacy through unbroken knowledge chain; zero extractiveness from non-performance

readings.commitment: The divine command kernel requires material performance; study without enactment is preparatory holding pattern awaiting Temple reconstruction
readings.authority_grounding: Biblical text specifies physical altar, specific location (Temple Mount), priestly lineage performing actual sacrifice; non-metaphorical reading of Torah law
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constraint remains unoccupied during Temple absence; current study is scaffold for future performance; victims are those obligated to sacrifice who cannot; extractiveness undefined until performance resumes

readings.commitment: Post-70 CE study preserves cultural memory of extinct practice; the commitment kernel is acknowledged as historically binding but presently inactive
readings.authority_grounding: Sociological/historical reading; rabbinic authority as cultural custodianship rather than active legal jurisdiction over unperformable law
readings.expected_structural_delta: No active constraint; study is archival labor; beneficiary is collective Jewish memory; victim set empty; constraint type collapses to ceremonial husk (D4)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Study-as-occupation holds that continuous study itself satisfies the divine command kernel; performance-prerequisite holds that only material sacrifice satisfies the kernel and study is preparatory. No single coherent framework can hold both: either study occupies the commitment or it does not.

Study-as-occupation claims the kernel remains actively binding via study; memorial-archival claims the kernel is historically binding but presently inactive. A framework cannot simultaneously hold a commitment as active and inactive.

Performance-prerequisite treats the kernel as dormant but still binding (awaiting conditions); memorial-archival treats it as extinct (binding only in historical sense). These are mutually exclusive temporal claims about the commitment's current normative force.

omegas.description: Does the performance_prerequisite reading treat Temple reconstruction as humanly achievable (political/engineering project) or messianically gated (divine intervention required)? If messianically gated, the constraint collapses to D4 despite performative framing.
omegas.source: Independence testing between performance_prerequisite and memorial_archival readings

omegas.description: Karaite Judaism rejected rabbinic authority and Oral Torah legitimacy. Did Karaite treatment of Kodashim post-70 CE differ structurally? If so, control case for whether study-as-occupation is rabbinic innovation or necessity given Temple absence.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — rabbinic authority benefits from study-as-occupation reading

omegas.description: Is this D1 (revision denial with covert drift accumulation) or already-collapsed D4 (ceremonial husk with revision-denial rhetoric)? The 1,900-year duration without drift-surfacing mechanism suggests D4, but rabbinic discourse maintains D1 framing. Boundary case.

Software preservation communities maintain 'digital archaeology' of obsolete platforms/languages with zero deployment. Structural analogue to Kodashim study? If parallel, suggests memorial_archival reading captures broader pattern of knowledge-preservation-as-legitimation.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) — model operating within assumption that religious law is categorically different from technical knowledge

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Three readings satisfy independence test (distinct observables, distinct authority groundings, mutually exclusive axioms). Kernel contest is genuine: study-as-occupation and performance-prerequisite cannot coexist in single coherent framework.
